newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT - Local HK banks seen outperforming.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Local HK banks seen outperforming.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said it expects local banks to beat consensus earnings expectations for the 1996 financial year due to robust growth in net interest income, higher interest margins and lower provision expenses.

In a recent report, regional head of financial institutions Andrew Brown said the biggest upside potential should come from Dah Sing Financial Holdings Ltd, HSBC Holdings Plc, FPB Bank Holdings Co and Wing Lung Bank Ltd.
He said Bank of East Asia Ltd's (BEA) 1996 earnings highlighted last year's healthy revenue environment and the positive resuls should be repeated by other banks.
Bank of East Asia posted a 14.5 percent rise in 1996 net profit to HK$1.88 billion from HK$1.64 million.
"In 1996, BEA reported a 21 percent increase in net interest income due to strong growth in loans and improved net interest margin. Such results are not unique to BEA," Brown said.

"We believe the net interest income growth for the sector will increase by 20 percent to 25 percent. As 75 percent to 85 percent of the sector's total revenue is driven by net interest income, we expect the bottom-line earnings results to see high year-to-year growth," he added.

"Going forward, obviously each bank will have a different margin experience unique to its own balance sheet, but with prime/HIBOR spread returning from sharp contraction in the second half of the year to more attractive levels, the year-to-year direction is distinctly upward."
Brown also said that higher-than-necessary first-half provisions should be lowered in the second half.
Wing Lung Bank said late on Wednesday it had posted net profit of HK$862 million for the year ended December 31, 1996, up 18.1 percent from the year before.
